title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: past Copilot chats appear in search results, with a Copilot Chats data source
summary: Hold: the briefing treats compliance retention as a documented limit on how far back users can search Copilot chats, but Microsoft has not documented that relationship. It also omits the retain-only exception to expiry-driven deletion and the same-location qualification for competing retention policies. The feature-specific default is not established, and Microsoft's retention command documentation gives conflicting parameter guidance.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot experiences retention location covers Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses for compliance.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].governs; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: How long compliance retention keeps interactions determines how far back users can search Copilot Chats.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot Chats" "search" "retention"' and '"Copilot Chats" conversations search licensing meter retention deleted results'; opened retention-policies-copilot, create-retention-policies and Search FAQ. None specifies the Copilot Chats search-history boundary.
claims.fix: Replace 'how long Copilot interactions are kept now also decides how far back users can search their own chats' with 'Retention policies govern compliance retention and deletion of Copilot interactions.' Remove 'and therefore findable' and 'and so how long past chats are kept' where they imply a search limit. Replace 'Retention is the control that bears on what users can find' with 'Retention governs stored Copilot interactions; Microsoft has not documented how it affects Copilot Chats search results.'

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: When messages expire under a retention policy, deletion is relayed to the Copilot app.
claims.quote: Content paths for retain-only retention policy ... If messages remain in your AI app after the retention period expires, nothing happens before and after the retention period; the message remains in its original location.
claims.fix: Qualify expiry-driven deletion throughout: 'For retain-and-delete or delete-only policies, expiry triggers backend deletion processes and a delete operation is relayed to the Copilot app; communication delays or caching can leave messages visible briefly. For retain-only policies, messages still in the app remain in their original location after expiry.' Do not describe every expired chat as deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Users can delete an associated chat in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat when that option is available.
claims.quote: Users delete (when this option is available) the associated chat in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: User-deleted or retention-expired chats may remain in Copilot Chats search results temporarily because of caching or deletion propagation.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot Chats" "search" "retention"' and '"Copilot Chats" conversations search licensing meter retention deleted results'; opened retention-policies-copilot and Search FAQ. Documented delays concern messages visible in the Copilot app, not search results.
claims.fix: Replace the search-results assertion with 'Microsoft documents that retention-triggered deletion can leave messages visible briefly in the Copilot app because of communication delays or caching. It does not state how quickly deleted chats disappear from Copilot Chats search results.' Remove the claim that this documented mechanism also covers user-deleted search results.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Messages visible in AI apps do not accurately establish compliance retention or permanent deletion, which should be verified with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: Use this section to understand how your compliance requirements are met by backend storage and processes, and should be verified by eDiscovery tools rather than by messages that are currently visible in your AI apps, such as Copilot.
